title: Saul Anointed and Made King
summary: The elders ask Samuel for a king; Saul son of Kish is anointed, defeats Nahash the Ammonite and is made king at Gilgal (1 Sam 8–11); he reigns forty years (Acts 13:21).
description: Judges-period record added from James B. Jordan's chronology (secondary display) with Ussher, Jones and, where available, CFAH-1 Table 1 dates for sorting. Jordan treats the judgeships as partly overlapping regional sequences (North / Centre / South) fitted to the 480 years of 1 Kgs 6:1 and the 300 years of Judg 11:26.

sorting_basis.note: Tier 3: Ussher-Jones (F. N. Jones): 1095 BC (no higher-tier year available). Jordan (secondary display) never sets the sort.

chronologies.date: "SAUL KING 1095 BC"; reigns 40 years to 1055 BC (Acts 13:21)
chronologies.citation: Jones, Chart No. 4 "Judges to the First 3 Kings" (© 1993 Floyd Jones; chart text revised "As of 2007"), timeline band
chronologies.note: Jones, 15th ed. (2002), ch. IV p. 53: "975 + 120 = 1095 BC (Saul begins to reign)".

chronologies.date: 2909c AM, 1095 BC (Saul made king; reigned 40 years, Acts 13:21)
chronologies.citation: Ussher, Annals of the World, Fourth Age §391 (paragraph numbering of the modern transcription)

chronologies.date: "2909 - Death of Abdon; Samuel appoints sons, rejected; anointing of Saul; accession of Saul. Saul is around 40. Jonathan is around 20." / "2910 - Saul year 1. Samuel is 49."
chronologies.citation: Jordan, From Creation to Solomon (Studies in Biblical Chronology No. 2, Biblical Horizons, Oct. 2001), ch. 11 "The Era of the Judges and the Reign of Saul", p. 52
chronologies.note: 2001 revision. Jordan's 1991 list (BC 3:8) has an earlier year; see the second Jordan entry. p. 49: "Saul was probably about 40 when he began to reign, reigned 40 years, and died at about 80 years of age." p. 45: 300 + 40 + 7 + 4 + 40 + 49 = 440 of the 480 years, "That leaves 40 years" for Saul.

chronologies.citation: Jordan, "Chronology and Kings (II)," Biblical Chronology 3:8 (August 1991), section "The Judges", summary list
chronologies.note: 1991 scheme, superseded by Jordan himself in 2001 (Studies in Biblical Chronology No. 2 dates the whole judges sequence 26 years later because he there ends the 300 years of Judg 11:26 when Ammon took the villages, AM 2860, not at Jephthah's victory). BC 5:2 (1993): "Saul became Israel's first official king in 2910, right after a sabbath year (2909)." BC 3:7: "34 years until Saul became king at the (adopted) age of one year. Samuel was 74." (1991; 2001 has Samuel about 49).
